claims.text: The starting eutectic high-entropy alloys have a coarse-grained microstructure.
The proposed powder-metallurgy intervention uses powder smaller than 10 μm, compaction at 500 MPa, and sintering at 1000°C.
The proposed powder-metallurgy intervention will refine the average grain size to below 1 μm.
The proposed processing route will homogenize the alloy microstructure.
Grain refinement and homogenization reduce dislocation density.
The increased grain-boundary area and reduced dislocation density enhance strength.
The increased grain-boundary area and reduced dislocation density enhance ductility.
Relative to conventionally cast eutectic high-entropy alloys, the intervention will increase yield strength by 20%.
Relative to conventionally cast eutectic high-entropy alloys, the intervention will increase elongation at break by 30%.
The proposed improvement should hold at operating temperatures below 500°C.
The proposed improvement should hold at applied stress levels up to 1000 MPa.
The magnitude of the strength and ductility improvements depends on alloy composition and processing conditions.
Failure to exceed a 15% yield-strength increase and a 25% elongation increase, or failure to achieve an average grain size of at most 1 μm, is specified as falsifying the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The conditions include stress levels 'up to 1000 MPa,' whereas the boundary requires stress below 1000 MPa, creating an inconsistency at exactly 1000 MPa.
